hints: Define a continuous zero-form function such as $f(x)=\cot x+x-1$.
Evaluate it at $x=2.5$ and at a larger convenient point below $\pi$, and use the sign change together with the stated uniqueness to place $\alpha$ above $2.5$.
walkthrough: Define the continuous function $f(x) = \cot x - (1 - x)$ on the interval $0 < x < \pi$.

Evaluate $f(x)$ at another point approaching $\pi$, for example $x = 3$:
$$\cot(3) = \dfrac{1}{\tan(3)} \approx \dfrac{1}{-0.142547} \approx -7.01525$$
$$1 - 3 = -2$$
$$f(3) = \cot(3) - (1 - 3) \approx -7.01525 - (-2) = -5.01525 < 0$$

Since $f(x)$ is continuous on $[2.5, 3]$ and changes sign from positive at $x = 2.5$ to negative at $x = 3$, by the Intermediate Value Theorem the unique root $\alpha$ must satisfy $2.5 < \alpha < 3$, which implies $\alpha > 2.5$.

hints: If the iteration converges, both $x_n$ and $x_{n+1}$ tend to the same limit $x$.
Set $x=\pi+\tan^{-1}(1/(1-x))$ and take tangent, respecting that the limit lies in $0<x<\pi$.
Rearrange to the defining equation $\cot x=1-x$, so uniqueness identifies the limit as $\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Assume the sequence converges to a limit $L$ in the interval $0 < L < \pi$. At convergence, setting $x_{n+1} = x_n = L$ gives:
$$L = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - L}\right)$$

Take the tangent of both sides:
$$\tan(L - \pi) = \dfrac{1}{1 - L}$$

Use the periodicity property of the tangent function, $\tan(\theta - \pi) = \tan\theta$:
$$\tan L = \dfrac{1}{1 - L}$$

Take reciprocals on both sides, recalling that $\cot L = \dfrac{1}{\tan L}$:
$$\cot L = 1 - L$$
Since $\alpha$ is the unique root of $\cot x = 1 - x$ in $0 < x < \pi$, the limit $L$ must be equal to $\alpha$.

hints: Choose a starting value above $2.5$ and apply the supplied formula in radian mode.
Record each result to 5 decimal places while using unrounded values in subsequent iterations.
Continue until the iterates establish a stable value to 3 decimal places.
walkthrough: Set up the iterative formula in radian mode: $x_{n+1} = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - x_n}\right)$.

Confirm the value to 3 decimal places by evaluating $f(x) = \cot x - (1 - x)$ across $[2.5755, 2.5765]$:
$$f(2.5755) = \cot(2.5755) - (1 - 2.5755) \approx -1.57321 - (-1.5755) = +0.00229 > 0$$
$$f(2.5765) = \cot(2.5765) - (1 - 2.5765) \approx -1.57805 - (-1.5765) = -0.00155 < 0$$
Since there is a sign change in the interval $(2.5755, 2.5765)$, the root rounds to 3 decimal places as:
$$\alpha = 2.576$$
